jinshu:053:p023.descriptorSuggestion: Son of Zhang Hua; companion to crown prince

value.event: Zhang Yi was the most renowned of the clan

jinshu:053:s0199.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。

translations.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.

jinshu:053:s0200.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。

translations.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.

jinshu:053:s0202.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。

translations.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

jinshu:053:s0203.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.

jinshu:053:s0204.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」

translations.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."
translations.idiomatic: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."

jinshu:053:s0205.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.

translations.literal: When Pei Du governed Taiyuan he appointed him as staff planner.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du governed Taiyuan he appointed Rong staff planner.

jiutangshu:166:s0309.zh: 時王承宗據鎮州叛，度請戎單車往諭之，承宗感泣受教。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Chengzong held Zhen Prefecture in rebellion; Du asked Rong to go alone in a single carriage to instruct him, and Chengzong wept and accepted instruction.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong held Zhen Prefecture in rebellion, Du asked Rong to go alone to instruct him, and Chengzong wept and accepted instruction.

jiutangshu:166:s0310.zh: 入為殿中侍御史，累拜吏部郎中，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He entered court as Palace Censor and was repeatedly promoted to Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel and then Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as palace censor, rose to bureau director of personnel, and became censor.

jiutangshu:166:s0311.zh: 尋為劍南東、西兩川宣慰使。

translations.literal: He was soon made pacification commissioner of the Eastern and Western Sichuan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made pacification commissioner of Eastern and Western Sichuan.

jiutangshu:166:s0312.zh: 西州承蠻寇之後，戎既宣撫，兼再定征稅，廢置得所，公私便之。

translations.literal: The western prefectures, having suffered barbarian raids, were both pacified by Rong and had their levies reassessed; abolitions and establishments were appropriate, and public and private alike benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Western prefectures, having suffered barbarian raids, were pacified by Rong; levies were reassessed, abolitions and establishments were appropriate, and public and private alike benefited.

jiutangshu:166:s0313.zh: 還，拜給事中，駁奏為當時所稱。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Drafting Attendant; his memorials of rejection were praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: On return he became drafting attendant; his memorials of rejection were praised at the time.

jiutangshu:166:s0314.zh: 改華州刺史，遷兗海沂密都團練觀察等使。

translations.literal: He was changed to governor of Hua Prefecture and transferred to overall training and surveillance commissioner of Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He became governor of Hua and overall training and surveillance commissioner of Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi.

jiutangshu:166:s0315.zh: 將行，州人戀惜遮道，至有解靴斷登者。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, the people, reluctant to part with him, blocked the road; some even pulled off boots and broke carriage steps.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, reluctant people blocked the road; some even pulled off boots and broke carriage steps.

jiutangshu:166:s0316.zh: 理兗一年，大和八年五月卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After governing Yan for one year he died in the fifth month of the eighth year of Dahe and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After governing Yan one year he died in the fifth month of Dahe 8 and was posthumously made minister of rites.

translations.literal: Zhang Zhengfu, styled Jianfang, was a native of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhengfu, styled Jianfang, was from Nanyang.

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dali was governor of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dali was governor of Fang Prefecture.

translations.literal: His grandfather Shaozhen was Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shaozhen was right vice director.

translations.literal: His father Ci was vice magistrate of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ci was vice magistrate of Suzhou.

jiutangshu:166:s0341.zh: 正甫登進士第，從樊澤為襄陽從事，累轉監察御史。

translations.literal: Zhengfu passed the jinshi examination, followed Fan Ze as staff in Xiangyang, and was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengfu passed the jinshi examination, followed Fan Ze as staff in Xiangyang, and rose to investigating censor.

translations.literal: When Yu Di replaced Ze he recruited and retained Zhengfu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Di replaced Ze he recruited and retained Zhengfu.

jiutangshu:166:s0343.zh: 正甫堅辭之，遂誣奏貶郴州長史。

translations.literal: Zhengfu firmly declined and was therefore falsely reported and demoted to Long Chief of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengfu firmly declined and was falsely reported and demoted to long chief of Chen Prefecture.

jiutangshu:166:s0344.zh: 後由邕府征拜殿中侍御史，遷戶部員外郎，轉司封員外、兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned from Yong prefecture staff as Palace Censor, promoted to Assistant in the Ministry of Revenue, and transferred to Assistant in the Bureau of Honors and concurrently Investigating Censor with charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later summoned from Yong staff as palace censor, he rose to assistant in the Ministry of Revenue and assistant in the Bureau of Honors with concurrent charge of investigating censor and miscellaneous affairs.

translations.literal: He was promoted to Bureau Director of the Ministry of Revenue and changed to metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to revenue bureau director and became metropolitan governor of Henan.

jiutangshu:166:s0346.zh: 由尚書右丞為同州刺史，入拜左散騎常侍、集賢殿學士判院事。

translations.literal: From Right Vice Director he became governor of Tong Prefecture; he entered court as Left Regular Attendant and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the academy.
translations.idiomatic: From right vice director he became governor of Tong; he entered court as left regular attendant and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the academy.

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of works.

jiutangshu:166:s0348.zh: 五年，檢校兵部尚書、太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Supervisory Minister of War and Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made supervisory minister of war and mentor of the heir apparent.

translations.literal: The next year he retired as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he retired as minister of personnel.

jiutangshu:166:s0350.zh: 正甫仁而端亮，蒞官清強。

translations.literal: Zhengfu was benevolent, upright, and bright; in office he was clear and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengfu was benevolent, upright, and bright; in office he was clear and forceful.

translations.literal: In outer appointments everywhere he went was praised as well governed.
translations.idiomatic: In outer appointments everywhere he went was praised as well governed.

jiutangshu:166:s0352.zh: 太和八年九月卒，年八十三，累贈太師。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth month of the eighth year of Taihe at the age of eighty-three and was repeatedly posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Taihe 8, aged eighty-three, and was repeatedly posthumously made grand preceptor.

translations.literal: His son was Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yifu.

translations.literal: Yifu passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu passed the jinshi examination.

jiutangshu:166:s0355.zh: 初正甫兄式，大歷中進士登第，繼之以正甫，式子元夫、傑夫、征夫又相次登科。

translations.literal: At first Zhengfu's elder brother Shi passed the jinshi in the Dalu era, followed by Zhengfu; Shi's sons Yuanfu, Jiefu, and Zhengfu in turn passed the examination in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhengfu's elder brother Shi passed the jinshi in the Dalu era, followed by Zhengfu; Shi's sons Yuanfu, Jiefu, and Zhengfu passed in succession.

jiutangshu:166:s0356.zh: 太和中，文章之盛，世共稱之。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era the flourishing of literary talent was praised together by the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era the flourishing of literary talent was praised by the age.

jiutangshu:166:s0357.zh: 元夫，太和初兵部郎中、知制誥，遷中書舍人，出為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuanfu, early in Taihe, was Bureau Director of the Ministry of War and drafting drafter, was promoted to Drafting Attendant, and was sent out as governor of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu, early in Taihe, was war bureau director and drafting drafter, rose to drafting attendant, and was sent out as governor of Ru.

jiutangshu:166:s0358.zh: 毅夫位至戶部侍郎、弘文館學士判院事。

translations.literal: Yifu rose to Vice Minister of Revenue and academician of the Hongwen Hall with charge of the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu rose to vice minister of revenue and Hongwen Hall academician with charge of the academy.

jiutangshu:166:s0359.zh: 諸群從登第者數人，而毅夫子祎最知名。

translations.literal: Several cousins passed the examination; among them Yifu's son Yi was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Several cousins passed the examination; among them Yifu's son Yi was most renowned.

The peer source identifies 張儀: 張儀者，魏人也。 始嘗與蘇秦俱事鬼谷先生，學術，蘇秦自以不及張儀。 張儀已學游說諸侯。 嘗從楚相飲，已而楚相亡璧，門下意張儀，曰：「儀貧無行，必此盜相君之璧。」 共執張儀，掠笞數百，不服，醳之。 其妻曰：「嘻！ 張儀謂其妻曰：「視吾舌尚在不？」 儀曰：「足矣。」 蘇秦已說趙王而得相約從親，然恐秦之攻諸侯，敗約後負，念莫可使用於秦者，乃使人微感張儀曰：「子始與蘇秦善，今秦已當路，子何不往游，以求通子之願？」 張儀於是之趙，上謁求見蘇秦。 蘇秦乃誡門下人不為通，又使不得去者數日。 已而見之，坐之堂下，賜仆妾之食。 張儀之來也，自以為故人，求益，反見辱，怒，念諸侯莫可事，獨秦能苦趙，乃遂入秦。 蘇秦已而告其舍人曰：「張儀，天下賢士，吾殆弗如也。 今吾幸先用，而能用秦柄者，獨張儀可耳。 然貧，無因以進。 乃言趙王，發金幣車馬，使人微隨張儀，與同宿舍，稍稍近就之，奉以車馬金錢，所欲用，為取給，而弗告。 張儀遂得以見秦惠王。 惠王以為客卿，與謀伐諸侯。 張儀曰：「賴子得顯，方且報德，何故去也？」 張儀曰：「嗟乎，此在吾術中而不悟，吾不及蘇君明矣！ 為吾謝蘇君，蘇君之時，儀何敢言。 且蘇君在，儀寧渠能乎！」 張儀既相秦，為文檄告楚相曰：「始吾從若飲，我不盜而璧，若笞我。 司馬錯與張儀爭論於惠王之前，司馬錯欲伐蜀，張儀曰：「不如伐韓。」 儀曰：「親魏善楚，下兵三川，塞什谷之口，當屯留之道，魏絕南陽，楚臨南鄭，秦攻新城、宜陽，以臨二周之郊，誅周王之罪，侵楚、魏之地。
